title: Backtest (classic): 'OPEC+ cut 2 mb/d, go long Brent'

input.event: OPEC+ just announced a 2 million barrels per day production cut from November, so go long Brent

excluded.op-013: outcome (EIA Brent spot after the decision; the excerpt date is the EIA page release date)
excluded.op-014: outcome (EIA Brent spot after the decision; the excerpt date is the EIA page release date)

pack_rule: Point-in-time pack = every excerpt in packs/opec2022.json dated on or before 2022-10-05 (op-001 to op-009). The pack was built by the evidence line from original pages (evidence branch 2553a9f); candidates that could not be verified were dropped there, with reasons in the pack's _provenance.dropped.

outcome.truth: Reuters' November survey (2022-12-01): OPEC pumped 29.01 mb/d, down 710,000 b/d month on month; the 10 members with quotas cut 720,000 b/d against a headline share of about 1.27 mb/d; Saudi Arabia delivered about 500,000 b/d (op-010 to op-012). EIA Brent spot: 94.35 on 10/5, 98.88 on 10/7, 99.87 on 11/7, 86.28 on 12/1, 76.37 on 12/9 (op-013, op-014). Other factors (demand, China's Covid policy, the Russian price cap) also moved prices, so the fall is not only about the cut.

observations.note: month-on-month fall in OPEC crude output in November, as a positive number (0.71 mb/d)

expected.behavior: Separate the quota cut from actual output: several members were already producing below quota (op-001, op-002, op-004), and analysts expected the physical cut to be about half the headline (op-007, op-008). The key dependency is the actual output of members with spare capacity; the deciding data (November production surveys) arrives in early December, so hold off on 10/5. Supporting excerpts (op-003, op-006, op-009) can be weighed, but the headline alone is not an entry signal.
expected.key_dependency_should_be: actual output cuts by members with spare capacity, not the headline quota cut

backtest.entry_resolution: A plan that waits for the November survey to show an actual cut of about 1 mb/d or more never enters (the survey showed 0.71). A plan that enters on price alone enters on 10/7.
backtest.grading_note: exit_met_by:2022-12-01 is the minimum acceptable path: a plan that entered must exit when the survey shows the cut fell short. Holding off from the start (entry never met) is the call the research note expects.

contamination_probe: Without any documents: after OPEC+ announced a 2 million barrels per day cut on October 5, 2022, how much did OPEC's actual output fall in November 2022, and where was Brent in early December 2022?
human_review: Backtest: is the key dependency actual output or the headline quota
E1: are op-001, op-007 and op-008 addressed
E2: does an entry condition wait for the November production data
notes: Classic case: contamination risk is medium (the cut is well known; the survey figures are less likely to be memorized). Report separately from R2 and R3. Backtests must run offline: the runner refuses --online for layer R; the pack holds only allowed_excerpts; the contamination probe runs first; citing anything outside allowed_excerpts counts as a leak.
